name: Student Residence Permit

qualifying_event.description: For foreign nationals admitted to a NOKUT-accredited Norwegian educational institution (university, university college, vocational, upper secondary, folk high school, or bible school).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Admission letter from a NOKUT-accredited institution; proof of funds (loans, grants, savings, or employment income).

requirements.blocker_text: Admission to an institution on NOKUT's (Norwegian Agency for Quality Assurance in Education) list of accredited institutions.
At least NOK 15,488/month or NOK 170,368/year in funds (loans, grants, savings, or employment income permitted).

evidence_required.document: Admission letter from a NOKUT-accredited institution
Proof of funds (NOK 170,368/year, or category-specific figure)

outcome.duration_length: tied to length of study programme (folk high school/bible school permits are 1 year, non-renewable)

sources.title: UDI -- Study permit: NOKUT-accreditation requirement, NOK 15,488/month (NOK 170,368/year) university/vocational funds figure, NOK 130,745/year folk high school and NOK 154,880/year bible school figures, 20 hrs/week work rights, permit duration tied to study length

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Norway). work_rights modeled 'restricted' per the confirmed 20 hours/week (full-time during holidays) allowance, which only starts once the permit is granted. leads_to_pr modeled FALSE and switchable_to excludes no_permanent_residence.json directly: the tier-1 source states time on a study permit 'generally does not count toward permanent residence eligibility' -- a materially different, stricter rule than most other countries in this dataset, where study time typically counts at least partially. Switching to a work or job-seeker permit after study is the actual path toward permanent residence.
